hypothesis: Explicit routing away from supplied-parent replies plus claim-status and progress rules will prevent standalone-post drift and unsupported outcome claims.
source_evidence: A supplied parent URL can make a shorthand post request a reply task.
Progress copy is strongest when it names a concrete change and user-visible effect.
Deadlines, awards, and outcomes are consequential and require current supplied evidence.
Aspirational language must not be presented as an official result.
changes: Added parent-URL routing to the reply skill.
Added progress change/effect and runtime-versus-supporting-artifact guidance.
Added confirmed, aspirational, and unknown claim statuses.
Added public-neutrality requirements and development evaluations.
rejected_alternatives: Adding posting automation was rejected because publication requires separate approval and a host adapter.
Embedding a fixed deadline, award, or account identifier was rejected because the package is portable.
expected_benefit: Cleaner selection between standalone posts and replies, with stronger evidence discipline.
regression_risk: Routing any request with a parent URL may be over-broad when quote text was intended; preserve the explicit form or ask.

evaluation.limitation: Analytical evidence only; no isolated runner was available.

applicability: Portable standalone X drafting; current platform facts require live verification when consequential.
